Using two results from Fourier's preprint, we show that if an $n$-element poset contains $X$ as an induced subposet, then, for every $k$ with $2\leq k\leq n-1$, its chain polytope has at least $\binom{n-3}{k-2}$ more $k$-dimensional faces than its order polytope, and that for every $n\geq5$ some $n$-element poset containing $X$ attains all these bounds at once. Since Hibi and Li showed that $\mathcal{O}(P)$ and $\mathcal{C}(P)$ are unimodularly equivalent exactly when $P$ does not contain $X$, this proves the equality statement for these values of $k$. The second version of Fourier's preprint gives an independent proof of this statement. For $k=1$, the equality statement is false: the polytopes $\mathcal{O}(X)$ and $\mathcal{C}(X)$ have the same number of edges (Hibi, Li, Sahara and Shikama) but are not unimodularly equivalent. Together with Fourier's inequality, these results settle the conjecture. The proofs given in this paper are formally verified in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Dave Goel

item.title: Separating hash families with large universe II
item.description: arXiv:2610.41353v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For fixed integers $t,k\ge 2$, put $N=(t-1)(k-1)+1$. We prove that the maximum universe size of a $t$-perfect hash family of length $N$ over an alphabet of size $q$ satisfies $ p_t(N,q)\ge q^{k-o(1)}$. Together with monotonicity in the length, this gives a positive answer to a question of Blackburn, Etzion, Stinson and Zaverucha for every choice of feasible parameters. Our proof combines the Nash--Williams--Tutte theorem, a graph-theoretic elimination argument, and a solution-free-set theorem established in our previous work.
item.dc:creator: Xin Wei, Gennian Ge

item.title: The Golden Quadruple: Four Reals Whose Differences Form a Geometric Progression, Rigidity of the Golden Ratio, and a Bohr Almost Periodic Cosine Sum
item.description:
arXiv:2611.00973v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$. The set $\{0,\varphi,\varphi^2,\varphi^3\}$ is classical (Euclid, Elements XIII.8): by $\varphi^2=\varphi+1$ its six pairwise differences take the values $1,\varphi,\varphi^2,\varphi^3$, with multiplicities $1,2,2,1$. We write it as the golden quadruple $S=(F, F-a, F-b, F-a-b)$, $a=\varphi u$, $b=\varphi^2u$, $F>a+b$, and study its extremal and rigidity properties. No five distinct reals have all their positive differences in $\{u\varphi^n:n\in\mathbb{Z}\}$; this follows from a result of Lenstra (1977), and we give a self-contained proof. We give an elementary proof of uniqueness: every four-element set with this property is a translate of $u\varphi^m\{0,\varphi,\varphi^2,\varphi^3\}$ for some $m\in\mathbb{Z}$, and if all its differences lie in $\{u,\varphi u,\varphi^2u,\varphi^3u\}$ it is a translate of $S$. Among all $x>1$, only $x=\varphi$ admits a four-point set of reals whose set of distinct differences is $\{c,cx,cx^2,cx^3\}$. For the analogous quadruple with base $x
eq\varphi$ the failure is measured by two closure residues, which along Fibonacci quotients equal $\pm u/\mathrm{Fib}_n^2$ and $\pm \mathrm{Fib}_{n+1}u/\mathrm{Fib}_n^3$. The cosine sum $C_S(t)=\sum\cos(2\pi d t)$ over the six differences equals $8\cos^2(\pi a t)\cos^2(\pi b t)-2$; it is not periodic but is Bohr almost periodic, with explicit almost periods $	au_n=\mathrm{Fib}_n/u$, and we determine the two-term asymptotics $\sup_t|C_S(t+	au_n)-C_S(t)|=6\sqrt3 \pi\varphi^{-n}-2\sqrt3 \pi^3\varphi^{-3n}+O(\varphi^{-5n})$, with optimal constants; the inclusion length of the $\varepsilon$-almost periods is of order $1/\varepsilon$. For a scale $K>0$ the golden ladder $
u_n=K\varphi^{-n}$ realises the construction with differences $
u_{200},\dots,
u_{203}$; we evaluate it for $K=\sqrt{c^5/(Gh)}$. All proofs are elementary and self-contained.
item.dc:creator: Micha{\l} Przybylski

item.title: Large fringe trees for random trees with given vertex degrees
item.description: arXiv:2604.06012v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper extends the study of fringe trees in random plane trees with a given degree statistic. While previous work established the asymptotic normality of the count of fringe trees isomorphic to a fixed tree, we investigate the case where the target tree grows with the size of the random tree. We consider three primary subtree counts: the number of fringe trees isomorphic to a specific growing tree, the number of fringe trees sharing a given growing degree statistic, and the number of fringe trees of a specific growing size. To establish our results, we employ and compare four distinct probabilistic frameworks: the method of moments with the Gao-Wormald theorem, Stein's method with coupling (to provide explicit error bounds in total variation distance), the Cai-Devroye method, and Stein's method with exchangeable pairs. Our findings provide conditions for Poisson and normal convergence for these subtree counts. Additionally, we provide a local limit theorem for sums of values obtained via sampling without replacement that may be of independent interest. Finally, our results and methods are also applied to conditioned critical Galton-Watson trees.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Berzunza Ojeda, Cecilia Holmgren, Svante Janson

item.title: Discrete homotopy groups of cubical sets
item.description: arXiv:2606.28693v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend the notion of discrete homotopy groups of graphs to arbitrary cubical sets, and show that the discrete homotopy groups of quasisymmetric cubical sets are naturally isomorphic to the homotopy groups of their geometric realizations. Here, quasisymmetric cubical sets are cubical sets equipped with coordinate permutation symmetries that are compatible with faces and degeneracies, but not necessarily with connections. We give a purely combinatorial construction of the left adjoint of the forgetful functor from the category of quasisymmetric cubical sets to the category of cubical sets, and prove that the unit of this adjunction is a natural weak equivalence. As a consequence, we obtain a purely combinatorial description of the homotopy groups of the geometric realizations of arbitrary cubical sets. As an application, we establish the discrete Hurewicz map from the discrete homotopy groups of a cubical set to the homology groups, and prove a Hurewicz theorem with respect to the discrete Hurewicz map whenever the cubical set is quasisymmetric. Applied to the 1-nerve of a directed graph, it also yields a Hurewicz theorem relating the homotopy groups of Li, Wu, Yau, and Zhang to singular cubical homology.
item.dc:creator: Daisuke Kishimoto, Yichen Tong

item.title: Many Antipodal Pairs Force Many Neighboring Pairs
item.description: arXiv:2608.02605v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $X=\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite set of points of diameter at most $1$. It is natural to expect that if many pairs $(x_i,x_j)$ lie at distance close to $1$ from each other, then some clustering phenomenon must occur, implying that a significant number of these pairs are also very close to each other. %For $0<\varepsilon<1$, we call a pair $(x_i,x_j)$ $\varepsilon$-antipodal if $\|x_i-x_j\|\ge 1-\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon$-neighboring if $\|x_i-x_j\|\le \varepsilon$. We prove that there exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that for all $0<\varepsilon<1$, whenever $n$ is large enough, we have: \[ \big|\{(i,j):\|x_i-x_j\|\le \varepsilon\}\big| \geq c\cdot \varepsilon^{1/2}\cdot \big|\{(i,j):\|x_i-x_j\|\geq 1-\varepsilon\}\big|. \] This confirms a recent conjecture of Steinerberger, who asked whether the $\varepsilon^{1/2}$ ratio is the best possible. We also study a two-parameter version of Steinerberger's question by considering the number of pairs at distance at most $\varepsilon_1$ and at distance at least $1-\varepsilon_2$. We show that in this case the optimal ratio is $\varepsilon_1^2\cdot\varepsilon_2^{-3/2}$ when $\varepsilon_1\leq\varepsilon_2$, and $\varepsilon_1^{1/2}$ otherwise. The proof proceeds by introducing an auxiliary graph associated with the set $X$ and reducing the problem to bounding the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix. Our main result is the outcome of human--AI interactions using ChatGPT 5.4.
item.dc:creator: G\'abor Dam\'asdi, Laurentiu Ploscaru

item.title: Max Independent Set Remains NP-hard when Excluding a Planar Induced Minor (and More)
item.description: arXiv:2609.11285v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that Max Independent Set (MIS) remains NP-hard in graphs excluding the $5 \times 5$ grid as an induced minor. This negatively answers a question of Dallard--Milani\v{c}--\v{S}torgel that has attracted sustained attention, and refutes a conjecture by Gartland and Lokshtanov. Unless $N$-variable 3-SAT can be solved in time $2^{\mathcal O(N^{1-\varepsilon})}$ for some $\varepsilon > 0$, MIS requires $2^{\Omega(n^{1/2-o(1)})}$ time on $n$-vertex graphs in this class. This complements a $2^{\widetilde{O}(n^{2/3})}$-time algorithm on any $H$-induced-minor-free class by Korhonen and Lokshtanov. Exploiting a connection between low twin-width or reduced parameters on one hand and planar-induced-minor-freeness on the other, we further show that 3-Coloring, Feedback Vertex Set and Dominating Set are NP-complete on weakly sparse graphs of reduced component max-leaf (hence twin-width) at most 3, even when a witnessing contraction sequence is given. Classes of bounded reduced component max-leaf (by any constant) and of twin-width at most 3 are known to exclude a fixed planar graph as an induced minor. The 3-Coloring and Feedback Vertex Set results refute more cases of the Gartland--Lokshtanov conjecture, even when the inputs are weakly sparse. The complexity of MIS in weakly sparse graphs excluding a planar induced minor remains open.
item.dc:creator: \'Edouard Bonnet, Yeonsu Chang

item.title: Polynomial-time Tensor Decomposition under the Kruskal Condition and the Lovitz--Petrov Generalization
item.description: arXiv:2609.13693v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An identifiability criterion is a condition on a tensor decomposition that certifies uniqueness when the condition holds. Kruskal's classical condition is one of the best-known deterministic criteria for identifiability. However, no polynomial-time decomposition algorithm is known under the Kruskal condition; verifying the condition itself is NP-hard. Lovitz and Petrov introduced a strictly more general identifiability condition which, in contrast, is polynomial-time verifiable, but no polynomial-time decomposition algorithm was known under this condition either. In this paper we give a randomized polynomial-time algorithm, in the algebraic model over $\mathbb R$, for tensor decomposition under the Lovitz--Petrov condition, and therefore also under the stricter Kruskal condition. Moreover, combining our algorithm with polynomial-time verification of the Lovitz--Petrov condition yields an efficient end-to-end certification procedure: after computing a decomposition, one can deterministically certify in polynomial time that it is unique and therefore of minimum rank.
item.dc:creator: Shiri Sivan

item.title: The Aldous chain on cladograms mixes in order $n^2$ steps
item.description: arXiv:2609.16955v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Cladograms of size $n$ are unrooted binary trees whose leaves are labelled from 1 to $n$. Aldous introduced in 2000 a Markov chain on cladograms, a step of which consists of removing a leaf uniformly at random and reinserting it on a uniformly chosen edge. We introduce a coupling for this walk, which follows multiple colored subtrees in parallel. We go around the lack of independence of the colored components by finding a relevant statistic, namely the sum of the squares of the sizes of all colored components, which we prove has a drift. We deduce that the mixing time of the walk is of order $n^2$, solving a conjecture of Aldous.
item.dc:creator: Valentin F\'eray, Lucas Teyssier

item.title: Kadison--Singer in Deterministic Polynomial Time
item.description: arXiv:2609.17266v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given rational Hermitian matrices $H_1,\dots,H_N$ of rank at most one, finds signs $s\in\{\pm1\}^N$ with $\|\sum_i s_i H_i\|\le 13\|\sum_i H_i^2\|^{1/2}$. As a corollary, for vectors $v_i$ with $\sum_i v_iv_i^*=I$ and $\|v_i\|^2\le\delta$, the signs yield a partition $[N] = S_1 \cup S_2$ such that each part satisfies $\|\sum_{i \in S_j} v_i v_i^* - \frac{I}{2}\| \leq \frac{13}{2}\sqrt\delta$ for $j = 1,2$. This gives a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for the Kadison--Singer problem, in Weaver's equivalent discrepancy-theoretic $\mathsf{KS}_2$ formulation, with a universal constant.
item.dc:creator: Ekene Ezeunala, Haotian Jiang

item.title: Vector Balancing in Polynomial Time
item.description: arXiv:2609.23540v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Koml\'os problem asks for signs $\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}^n$ with $\|A\varepsilon\|_\infty$ bounded by an absolute constant whenever the columns of $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ have Euclidean norm at most $1$. We give the first polynomial-time algorithm for this problem in the unit-cost real-RAM model. Our deterministic algorithm achieves discrepancy at most $8272$. As a consequence, we obtain a deterministic $O(\sqrt t)$-discrepancy algorithm for the Beck-Fiala problem on set systems in which each element belongs to at most $t$ sets. Our algorithm rounds a fractional coloring while keeping the row sums bounded. Its key idea is to keep the number of nearly tight row constraints small relative to the number of active coordinates. We achieve this through a spectral bound based on a weighted Gram matrix of squared row entries. We maintain the bound using a cubic spectral potential and negative-curvature updates that satisfy the required linear constraints.
item.dc:creator: Shengtao Guo, Ethan X. Fang, Junwei Lu

item.title: QPTAS for Max Weight Independent Set in Graphs with Strongly Edge-Sublinear Separators
item.description: arXiv:2610.16025v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A hereditary graph class has strongly edge-sublinear separators if, for some constant $0 \leqslant b < 1$, every graph in the class with $m$ edges admits a balanced separator of size $\mathcal O(m^b)$. We show that Max Weight Independent Set (MWIS) admits a deterministic quasipolynomial-time approximation scheme (QPTAS) on every such class. In particular, this applies to graphs excluding any fixed graph as an induced minor, by a separator theorem of Korhonen and Lokshtanov [SODA 2024]. Our theorem generalizes the QPTASes for axis-parallel rectangles [Adamaszek and Wiese, FOCS 2013] and polygons [Adamaszek, Har-Peled, and Wiese, JACM 2019], or equivalently for packing connected subgraphs of a planar graph [Pilipczuk, van Leeuwen, and Wiese, Algorithmica 2020]. It also generalizes the QPTAS for MWIS on hereditary classes with strongly sublinear separators measured in vertices [Dvo\v{r}\'ak, EJC 2018; Dvo\v{r}\'ak and Lahiri, ESA 2021], as well as the QPTASes for graphs excluding specific induced minors [Chudnovsky et al., arXiv 2025; Bonnet et al., SWAT 2026; Czy\.zewska et al., arXiv 2026].
item.dc:creator: \'Edouard Bonnet, Yeonsu Chang

item.title: Asymptotic Rank of Weighted Graph Tensors via Completely Positive Covers
item.description: arXiv:2610.34273v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a conic upper bound on the asymptotic rank of every weighted graph tensor over every field. If $W$ is the logarithmic edge-weight matrix of its dimension matrix $Q$, then $$ \operatorname{MaxCut}(W)\le\log_2\operatorname{\widetilde R}_{\mathbb F}(\operatorname{WT}(Q))\le U_{\operatorname{CP}}^{\Delta}(W). $$ Here $U_{\operatorname{CP}}^{\Delta}(W)$ maximizes $\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}W_{i,j}P_{i,j}$ over nonnegative symmetric zero-diagonal matrices $P$ such that $J-2P$ is copositive and $P_{i,j}\le P_{i,k}+P_{k,j}$ for all distinct vertices. The matrix $J$ is all-one, and copositivity means nonnegativity of the quadratic form on nonnegative vectors. Our starting point extends OpenAI's polynomial multiplication method and its subsequent arbitrary-field developments from three tensor legs to arbitrary order. We prove $$ \left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\right\rfloor\le\log_2\operatorname{\widetilde R}_{\mathbb F}(\operatorname{GT}_2(K_n))\le\frac{n^2}{4}. $$ The edge exponent is at most $n/(2(n-1))$ and tends to the optimal value $1/2$, improving the previous Coppersmith--Winograd bounds and answering Question 1.3.1 of Christandl, Vrana, and Zuiddam. The bounds coincide for every even $n$. For every odd $m\ge3$, the theorem gives $\log_2\widetilde R_{\mathbb F}(\operatorname{GT}_2(C_m))\le m-1+1/(m+1)$, improving the previous cycle bound with a gap of only $1/(m+1)$ above the maximum cut. On weighted triangles, the program recovers the rectangular matrix multiplication curve of Uzna\'nski and Amanov, van den Berg, and Zuiddam. The CP and semidefinite programs, with or without path constraints, all have value $9/4$ on the unweighted triangle, giving this upper bound a natural conic interpretation. Further applications give explicit bounds for complete multipartite graphs, split graphs, and wheels, including new cases of maximum-cut equality.

item.title: Low-rank matrices with three prescribed off-diagonal values over $\mathbb{F}_p$
item.description: arXiv:2610.39908v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For every prime $p$ and every three-element set $L\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p$, we prove that, for every integer $n\geq1$, there exists a symmetric $n\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with zero diagonal, off-diagonal entries in $L$, and rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. This answers a question of Bukh. When $0\notin L$, a standard polynomial argument shows that the exponent $1/3$ is optimal. The proof combines an incidence matrix factorization with a projective-plane construction controlling line-intersection numbers modulo $p$. A separate geometric construction in characteristic two yields better explicit constants in certain cases, and also gives integer lifts $L'$ of the prescribed sets $L$ and symmetric $L'$-matrices of rational rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. When $0\notin L'$, this improves Bukh's general quadratic lower bound, giving matrices of order $\Omega_{p,L}(r^3)$ and rational rank at most $r$.

item.title: Optimality of the $D_4$ lattice quantizer
item.description: arXiv:2611.00100v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the root lattice $D_4$ uniquely minimizes the normalized second moment among four-dimensional lattices, up to similarity. The minimum is $13/(120\sqrt{2})$. The proof reduces the problem to polynomial inequalities on three secondary cones. We derive the second-moment formulas geometrically and give explicit polynomial certificates that can be checked by coefficient comparison. We also derive a lower bound for lattice quantizers in every dimension at least two from the number of Voronoi facets, using a comparison with circular cones and concavity in the solid angle. This bound strictly improves the sphere bound and recovers the hexagonal value in dimension two.
item.dc:creator: Tianle Liu

item.title: Finite groups with all involutions fused
item.description: arXiv:2611.03366v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We characterize finite groups whose involutions form a single fusion class. In the solvable case, we show that the $2$-length is $1$, extending Thompson's theorem which states that a solvable group with all involutions conjugate has $2$-length $1$. For a nonsolvable group $G$, we prove that if its involutions are fused then they are conjugate; moreover, $G/\mathbf{O}_{2'}(G)$ is almost quasisimple. As an application, we obtain a restriction on $m$ for which an $m$-pyramidal Kirkman triple system can be realized under a nonsolvable group.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Guo, Yan Zhou Zhu
